etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English nacioun, nacion, from Old French nacion, from Latin nātiōnem, accusative of nātiō (“nation”). Displaced native Old English þēod.

definitions.definition: (by extension, informal, often humorous) A community united by some trait (especially an interest) but not historically constituted.

quote.citation: 2016 May 5, Johansson Anna, “5 Marketing Tips for Reaching the DIY Generation”, in Entrepreneur‎[1], retrieved 2023-12-21:
quote.text: Did Pinterest create a culture of do-it-yourselfers, or did the DIY nation create Pinterest? The answer may not be certain, but we do know that a lot of customers love to do things on their own.

definitions.definition: (collective) A historically constituted, stable community of people, formed based on a common language, territory, economic life, ethnicity and/or psychological make-up manifested in a common culture.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 22:27:
quote.text: All the ends of the woꝛld ſhall remember, and turne vnto the Lord: and all the kinreds of the nations ſhall woꝛſhip befoꝛe thee.

definitions.definition: (international law, metonymically) A sovereign state; (loosely, metonymically, proscribed) a country.

quote.citation: 2013 June 7, David Simpson, “Fantasy of navigation”, in The Guardian Weekly‎[2], volume 188, number 26, page 36:
quote.text: It is tempting to speculate about the incentives or compulsions that might explain why anyone would take to the skies in [the] basket [of a balloon]:  […]  perhaps to muse on the irrelevance of the borders that separate nation states and keep people from understanding their shared environment.

definitions.definition: (chiefly historical) An association of students based on the birthplace or ethnicity of its members.
(obsolete) A great number; a great deal.

quote.citation: 1762, Laurence Sterne, The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman, new edition, volume V, Altenburgh: G. E. Richter, published 1772, page 57:
quote.text: […] and what a nation of herbs he had procured to mollify her humours, &c. &c. […]

definitions.definition: In North America, an Indigenous people and  their federally recognized territory.

quote.citation: 1884 December 10, Mark Twain [pseudonym; Samuel Langhorne Clemens], chapter XIX, in The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn: (Tom Sawyer’s Comrade) […], London: Chatto & Windus, […], →OCLC, page 186:
quote.text: “Looky here, Bilgewater,” he says, “I’m nation sorry for you, but you ain’t the only person that’s had troubles like that.”
